samples.summary: Route-collision guard never asserts that it actually collected any routes
samples.evidence: The collision loop only asserts `expect(collisions).toEqual([])` (line 78). If route enumeration silently yields nothing — a Nest version change to `PATH_METADATA`/`METHOD_METADATA`, decorated handlers not visible via `Object.getOwnPropertyNames(proto)`, or `suffix === undefined` short-circuiting on every handler (line 63) — the spec passes green while checking zero routes. The only sanity guard is `controllers.length >= 18` (line 42), which proves controllers were found, not routes. Since this spec is the sole regression guard for the `tabs/:tabId/move` shadowing bug this diff works around (`tabs.controller.ts` uses `reorder` because of it), a vacuous detector would let the same class of silently-shadowed endpoint ship again. A `expect(seen.size).toBeGreaterThan(N)` would close it.
searchedFor: grep for other route/collision specs in packages/backend

samples.summary: New CRDT read/write paths are only tested against hand-rolled proxy fakes; no attached-Yorkie e2e like the existing docs-tree one
samples.evidence: comment-ops.spec.ts simulates the Yorkie proxy semantics the implementation depends on with hand-written stand-ins: a `Proxy` faking a non-`Array.isArray` comment list (comment-ops.spec.ts 'reads a thread whose comment list is not a real array'), a `deleteProperty` proxy faking `RHTPQMap.deleteByKey` throwing 'fail to find <key>', and `toJSON`-returning-a-string objects in worksheet-images.controller.spec / tabs.controller.spec. Every one of these encodes an assumption about real Yorkie behaviour (Long/bigint timestamps, delete-on-missing-key, array proxies, raw-JSON control characters) that the tests themselves assert rather than observe. packages/backend/test/docs-tree-attached.e2e-spec.ts exists precisely because 'the colocated docs-tree.spec.ts ... bypasses the proxy semantics'; no equivalent attached spec was added for comment-ops, board-tree, worksheet-images or the tab `duplicate`/`unwrapJson` path (I globbed packages/backend/test/**). If any assumption is wrong the whole comments API 500s or writes 1970 dates against a live document and nothing in the suite notices.

samples.summary: 18 new HttpClient methods have no test asserting their URL, verb or body — the CLI suite mocks HttpClient away entirely
samples.evidence: class-b-commands.test.ts replaces the whole `HttpClient` class with a stub (`vi.mock('../src/client/http-client.js', ...)`), so it can only prove which client method a command calls and with what arguments. The dry-run assertions in that file (e.g. `url: ${BASE}/documents/doc-1/tabs/tab-1/duplicate`) exercise the path string duplicated in the command's `printDryRun` call, not the one in http-client.ts. I grepped packages/cli/test for `moveTab|deleteTab|duplicateTab|listComments|addSlide|getWorksheetImages` and class-b-commands.test.ts is the only hit; http-client-paths.test.ts covers only pre-existing methods. A wrong path or verb in e.g. `moveTab` (POST `.../reorder`, deliberately not `.../move`) or `deleteComment` ships green and 404s for users.

samples.summary: Board getContent test mocks the Yorkie callback away, so readBoardRoot never runs in the controller path
samples.evidence: 'returns the board content JSON for a board-typed document' does `yorkieService.withDocument.mockResolvedValue(board)` and then asserts `getContent(...)` equals `board` — the callback `(doc) => readBoardRoot(doc.getRoot())` is never invoked, so the assertion holds no matter what the read callback does. It does meaningfully pin `docKeyPrefix: 'board-'` and `syncMode: 'readonly'`. readBoardRoot itself is covered by board-tree.spec.ts, so the residual gap is the wiring of reader→route only.
searchedFor: read the board describe block in docs-content.controller.spec.ts

samples.summary: applyDelete's 'worksheet may not exist' branch (datasource/lakehouse tabs) is untested
samples.evidence: `applyDelete` guards `if (root.sheets?.[tabId]) delete root.sheets[tabId]` for tabs that have metadata but no worksheet (datasource / lakehouse), but tab-ops.spec.ts only deletes a sheet tab created via `createTab`, and tabs.controller.spec.ts's `remove` describe has no datasource case (the only datasource fixture is in the `duplicate` describe). Nothing exercises deleting a non-sheet tab end to end.
searchedFor: read the new resolveDelete/applyDelete blocks in tab-ops.spec.ts
read the remove describe in tabs.controller.spec.ts

samples.summary: The non-slides type gate is only tested for `add`; layouts/duplicate/move/remove are untested for it
samples.evidence: 'refuses a non-slides document before opening Yorkie' calls only `controller.add`. `layouts`, `duplicate`, `move` and `remove` each call `assertSlidesDocument` independently; if one of those calls were dropped, a sheet or doc id would reach `withDocument` with the slides docKey prefix and no test would fail. Same shape of gap in worksheet-images.controller.spec.ts, where only `setImages` is checked against a non-sheet document and `getImages` is not.

samples.summary: `sheets images set` stdin branch is never exercised
samples.evidence: class-b-commands.test.ts only drives `images set` with `--data`. The `for await (const chunk of process.stdin)` branch (and its 'on stdin' error wording) is untested, even though piping `images get` output into `images set` is the documented round-trip the command is designed for.

samples.summary: `expect(threads[0].createdAt).toEqual(expect.any(Number))` cannot detect the 32-bit timestamp truncation it appears to guard
samples.evidence: In 'lists threads across every tab', the createdAt assertion passes for any number, including the 1970-era value produced by the Yorkie int32 truncation that toYorkieMs/fromYorkieMs exist to prevent. The value-level check does exist in comment-ops.spec.ts ('stores timestamps as Long...'), so this is a weak assertion rather than an uncovered behaviour.

samples.summary: Controller-level guard `if (!Number.isSafeInteger(actorId) || actorId <= 0) return;` in notify() is untested
samples.evidence: comments.controller.spec.ts's notification describe always uses numeric author ids (7, 9), so the early return for a non-numeric/zero actor id never executes. The equivalent rule is covered in packages/sheets/src/comment/__tests__/notify-plan.test.ts ('plans nothing for an actor that is not a real user id'), so the duplicate backend guard is the only untested part.
searchedFor: read the notifications describe in comments.controller.spec.ts

finding.summary: New CRDT read/write paths are only tested against hand-rolled proxy fakes; no attached-Yorkie e2e like the existing docs-tree one
finding.evidence: comment-ops.spec.ts simulates the Yorkie proxy semantics the implementation depends on with hand-written stand-ins: a `Proxy` faking a non-`Array.isArray` comment list (comment-ops.spec.ts 'reads a thread whose comment list is not a real array'), a `deleteProperty` proxy faking `RHTPQMap.deleteByKey` throwing 'fail to find <key>', and `toJSON`-returning-a-string objects in worksheet-images.controller.spec / tabs.controller.spec. Every one of these encodes an assumption about real Yorkie behaviour (Long/bigint timestamps, delete-on-missing-key, array proxies, raw-JSON control characters) that the tests themselves assert rather than observe. packages/backend/test/docs-tree-attached.e2e-spec.ts exists precisely because 'the colocated docs-tree.spec.ts ... bypasses the proxy semantics'; no equivalent attached spec was added for comment-ops, board-tree, worksheet-images or the tab `duplicate`/`unwrapJson` path (I globbed packages/backend/test/**). If any assumption is wrong the whole comments API 500s or writes 1970 dates against a live document and nothing in the suite notices.

verdict.reason: The absence itself is real (no backend attached-Yorkie spec imports comment-ops; I globbed **/*attached*, **/*e2e*.ts, **/*.integration.ts and grepped comment-ops/listThreads/applySetResolved repo-wide), but it is not blocking under the test-adequacy rubric, which excludes "add more tests" unless the behavior lacks any meaningful test. (1) comment-ops.spec.ts is not vacuous or over-mocked: the module under test and the @wafflebase/sheets engine are real, and each proxy stand-in locks a concrete regression — removing the array-likeness guard fails comment-ops.spec.ts:117-120, removing the resolvedAt presence guard fails :169-171. comments.controller.spec.ts:30-38,88-118 drives the real controller plus real comment-ops over a root the update callback truly mutates. (2) The claimed impact ("if any assumption is wrong the comments API 500s") does not follow: both simulated assumptions are implemented defensively in both directions — isThread (comment-ops.ts:125-130) accepts array-likeness, true for real arrays and CRDT proxies alike, and applySetResolved (comment-ops.ts:298-307) deletes only keys that are present, safe whether or not RHTPQMap.deleteByKey throws. (3) The one assumption with user-visible consequences, Long/bigint timestamps, IS observed against a live Yorkie server: document-copy-attached.e2e-spec.ts:69-70 writes BigInt(1_780_000_000_000) and :125-126 asserts it round-trips ("a 32-bit Integer would have decoded as a 1970 timestamp"), with control-character raw-JSON handling at :61-64,121; CI enables these gated specs (.github/workflows/ci.yml:589). The same thread shape (comments array push/splice, delete of resolvedAt/resolvedBy on a live proxy, map delete, bigint stamps) is exercised against a real yorkie.Document in packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/comments/yorkie-comment-store.test.ts:165-196,199-222. So the gap is a fidelity/depth ask over already-meaningful coverage, not a behavior shipping untested.
